title: Odd Numbers in a Closed Range
statement:
You get two non-negative integers low and high with low ≤ high. Return how many odd numbers lie between them, including both ends.

The range can be up to a billion numbers wide, so walking through it is not an option.

examples.why: The range holds only 6, which is even.
3, 5 and 7. Halving the width (7 − 3) / 2 = 2 misses one, because both ends are odd.

gen: (r, big) => { if (big) { const lo = r.int(0, 1000); return [lo, 1000000000 - r.int(0, 1)]; } const lo = r.int(0, 30); return [lo, lo + r.int(0, 20)]; }
hints: How many odd numbers are there from 1 up to some x? Try a few small x and look for a formula.
The odd numbers in [0, x] number ⌊(x + 1) / 2⌋.
Count up to high, then subtract the count up to low − 1, which is ⌊low / 2⌋.

explain.intuition:
Counting in a range is easiest as "count up to high" minus "count up to just below low", the same prefix trick as prefix sums. Up to x, every pair (0, 1), (2, 3), … holds one odd number, so there are ⌊(x + 1) / 2⌋ odd numbers in [0, x].

So the answer is ⌊(high + 1) / 2⌋ − ⌊low / 2⌋, which handles every parity of the two ends without any special cases.
pitfalls: Using (high − low) / 2. It is off by one when both ends are odd.
Looping from low to high; with a range of a billion that is far too slow for an O(1) question.
Mixing up the two prefix bounds: the count below low is ⌊low / 2⌋, not ⌊(low + 1) / 2⌋, or an odd low is lost.

solutions.title: Half the width, then fix the ends
solutions.idea: A range of w = high − low + 1 numbers alternates parity, so it holds w / 2 odd numbers, rounded up only when it starts on an odd number.

solutions.title: Prefix counts
solutions.idea: Odd numbers up to high, minus odd numbers below low.
